subject: Physics
source: Edexcel (Pearson) GCSE (9-1) Physics 1PH0 specification (2016 onwards) — Y10 covered topics 1–7 (Key concepts; Motion and forces; Conservation of energy; Waves; Light and the EM spectrum; Radioactivity; Astronomy).

specPoints.specTitle: Use of SI base units and derived units; orders of magnitude and standard form
Significant figures, precision and accuracy; uncertainty in measurements
Distance, displacement, speed, velocity; calculations using v = s/t and average speed
Acceleration: a = (v – u)/t; equations of motion and v² = u² + 2as (HT only for v² = u² + 2as)
Distance-time and velocity-time graphs: gradient interpretation; area under graph as displacement (HT for non-uniform acceleration)
Newton's laws of motion: 1st (inertia), 2nd (F = ma), 3rd (action-reaction); applied to everyday situations
Stopping distance: thinking distance + braking distance; factors affecting each
Momentum: p = mv; conservation of momentum in collisions (HT only — derivation of force as rate of change of momentum)
Energy stores and transfers; conservation of energy; closed systems
Calculations: KE = ½mv², GPE = mgh, work done W = Fd, power P = E/t and P = Fv (HT only for P = Fv)
Efficiency = useful output / total input; ways of reducing wasted energy transfers
Energy resources: renewable and non-renewable; advantages and limitations of each
Wave properties: amplitude, wavelength, frequency, period; wave equation v = fλ; transverse vs longitudinal waves
Reflection, refraction and absorption of waves at boundaries between materials
Sound waves: longitudinal nature; range of human hearing; ultrasound applications
Electromagnetic spectrum: radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma; uses and dangers of each
Production and detection of EM waves; refraction by lenses (HT only — drawing ray diagrams for converging and diverging lenses)
Atomic structure: nucleus, protons, neutrons, electrons; isotopes; nuclide notation
Radioactive decay: alpha, beta-minus, beta-plus (HT only), gamma; nuclear equations and properties
Half-life: definition, calculations including using a graph; activity and count rate
Hazards of ionising radiation: irradiation vs contamination; medical and industrial uses; precautions
Solar system: Sun, planets, dwarf planets, moons; structure of the universe; orbits as ellipses
Life cycle of stars: nebula → main sequence → red giant or supergiant → white dwarf, neutron star or black hole; element formation
Red shift and the expanding universe; evidence for the Big Bang theory (HT only — quantitative red-shift reasoning)
Core Practical: Investigate the relationship between force, mass and acceleration using a trolley and light gates
Core Practical: Investigate how the extension of a spring depends on the force applied (Hooke's law); identify limit of proportionality
Core Practical: Investigate the wave properties (frequency, wavelength, speed) of a wave in a ripple tank or on a stretched string
